questions.knowledge_point: Stating the Vertex of a Vertical Parabola Given Its Equation in Standard Form
questions.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola ${x}^{2}=4(y-2)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=0$ and $k=2.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $(0,2).$

questions.knowledge_point: Stating the Vertex of a Vertical Parabola Given Its Equation in Standard Form
questions.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola ${x}^{2}=-\frac{3}{2}(y-1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-0)^{2} & =4(-\frac{3}{8})(y-1).\end{aligned}
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=-\frac{3}{8}.$

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=0$ and $k=1.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $(0,1).$

questions.knowledge_point: Stating the Vertex of a Horizontal Parabola Given Its Equation in Standard Form
questions.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola ${y}^{2}=-32x?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola that has its vertex at the origin is

$$
{y}^{2}=4px,
$$

where $p$ is a constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as 

$$
{y}^{2}=4(-8)x.
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=-8.$ Therefore, our parabola has its vertex at $(0,0).$
